businessCases.description: Used for any form of initial request, submission, or formal application initiated by a private or corporate party.
Used for an official, authoritative call for action, a formal summons, or a mandatory request issued by an authority.
Used for supplementary, secondary, or alternative applications within the same announcement type to prevent duplicate keys.
Used for early, informal public involvement, consultations, or feedback phases prior to formal decrees.
Used for the formal, statutory public exposure of plans or documents where objection periods are legally triggered.
Used for the official publication, issuance, or service of legal documents, regulations, or decrees.
Used for any subsequent amendment, modification, or mutation of an existing register entry, document, or project.
Used when an entire process is repeated, completely revised, or a licence is generally renewed.
Used for the official granting of a personal or corporate licence, permit, or professional entitlement.
Used for granting supplementary or auxiliary permissions tied to an existing licence.
Used when a provisional status, agreement, or democratic election is formally confirmed, ratified, or adopted.
Used specifically for optional or mandatory referendum periods and related public popular vote procedures.
Used for formal administrative warnings, reminders, or default notices.
Used when an application, permit, or legal request is formally denied or rejected by the authorities.
Used for the temporary freezing, halting, or pausing of an active right, procedure, or professional licence.
Used for the formal, permanent withdrawal or revocation of any granted title, operating licence, or official right.
Used when a procedure or application is actively cancelled, aborted, or retracted by the initiating party.
Used when a procedural step formally fails or does not meet its legal threshold.
Used for the official designation or assignment of individuals, bodies, administrators, or representatives.
Used specifically for administrative rulings and decisions issued regarding formal public objections.
Used for judicial rulings and higher-instance decisions resulting from legal appeals.
Used when a higher authority or supervisory body formally approves or validates a decision.
Used for the official entry into force, enactment, or executive execution of a final regulation or measure.
Used for the regular, formal conclusion and closing of an entire administrative, judicial, or insolvency file.
Used as a generic fallback key for standard public announcements or information notices without specific workflows.
A specific administrative decree or ruling concerning environmental impact assessments within construction or spatial planning procedures.
A property registry mutation or transfer of ownership specifically triggered by a contract of purchase and sale.
A property registry mutation or transfer of ownership resulting from a formal deed of gift.
A property registry mutation or transfer of ownership resulting from the division of an estate.
A property registry mutation based on a matrimonial property agreement or divorce decree.
A property registry mutation representing miscellaneous forms of legal property transfers.
A property registry mutation or transfer of ownership explicitly ordered by a court judgment.
A formal public design or ideas competition launched by a public authority.
A selective procurement procedure involving parallel study commissions.
The automatic or legal loss of a professional licence or patent due to the failure to meet ongoing criteria.
The official opening of bankruptcy proceedings following a failed composition moratorium or restructuring attempt.
The official opening of bankruptcy proceedings directed against a deceased person's estate.
The official opening of bankruptcy and liquidation proceedings regarding an estate that has been rejected by all legal heirs.
A public auction of real estate or assets triggered by a standard debt enforcement and asset seizure procedure.
A public auction of real estate or assets conducted within the framework of a formal bankruptcy liquidation.
A public auction explicitly ordered by a civil court to resolve co-ownership disputes or estate divisions.
A public auction specifically dedicated to movable assets and personal property, such as vehicles, equipment, or art.
A public auction carried out voluntarily by the owner but executed through official authorities.
The immediate suspension or closure of bankruptcy proceedings due to a total lack of realizable assets to cover the procedural costs.
A formal public notice or call issued to locate unknown or missing heirs regarding an open probate case.
A statutory public call issued to creditors to submit their financial claims within liquidation, bankruptcy, or corporate capital reduction procedures.
The formal public exposure and inspection period of both the schedule of claims and the asset inventory within a bankruptcy file.
The formal public inspection period dedicated exclusively to the bankruptcy schedule of claims.
The formal public inspection period dedicated exclusively to the official asset inventory of a bankruptcy or estate case.
The formal public exposure of the final distribution list and the final administrative account in a bankruptcy liquidation.
The formal public inspection period of the schedule of burdens listing encumbrances and liens on real estate.
The formal public exposure of the schedule of claims within composition proceedings involving an assignment of assets.
The formal public inspection period of the accountability or management report submitted by a liquidator or administrator.
The formal public inspection period of the final report concluding a liquidation or bankruptcy procedure.
The formal public exposure of a provisional or interim distribution list prior to the final distribution of assets.
The official entry into force or announcement of a judicial prohibition against unauthorized parking or access on private property.
The official entry into force or announcement of a judicial prohibition against unauthorized storage or dumping on private land.
A judicial summons or court order demanding a party to appear in court specifically for a bankruptcy hearing.
A judicial summons demanding a party to appear before a civil conciliation authority or peace officer.
A formal court order demanding the defendant to file a statement of defence or legal answer within a specific deadline.
A formal court order demanding a party to pay a monetary advance on court fees or procedural costs.
A formal judicial request ordering a party or third party to produce specific documents, records, or physical evidence.
